headline: Southborough prepared for a potential FY28 tax override, set its FY27 tax rate, and advanced major development and school building plans.
synopsis: Southborough municipal and school officials began confronting an early FY28 operating budget deficit of $1.4 million, drafting dual budget scenarios that pair a potential Proposition 2 1/2 override against sharp service and staffing cuts. For the current fiscal year, the Select Board finalized property taxes by adopting a single tax rate of $14.54 per thousand. Architects informed town building committees that renovating Neary Elementary School will cost between $33 million and $40 million, rendering an earlier $15 million budget estimate unfeasible. In land use and development, the Planning Board continued detailed site plan hearings for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse, while the Select Board voted to sponsor a warrant article lifting the town's cap on 55-plus housing. Additionally, the town secured an up to $632,000 state grant to fund half of the planned Harold E. Fay Memorial Park improvements.

top_items.title: Town projects $1.4 million FY28 deficit and weighs operating override
top_items.why: Level-service budgets leave a $1.4 million shortfall that would require a Proposition 2 1/2 tax override, while level-funding would trigger deep departmental service and staff cuts.
top_items.body: Town administration and municipal boards opened reviews of the fiscal year 2028 operating budget under two competing tracks. Budget A maintains existing town and school services but produces an estimated $1.4 million deficit requiring voter approval of a Proposition 2 1/2 override. In contrast, level-funded Budget B would force severe reductions across municipal services, including eliminating roughly 15 school staff positions, cutting a police officer and dispatcher, and reducing fire department shift staffing, which would halt routine operation of the town's second revenue-generating ambulance.

top_items.title: Select Board adopts single FY27 property tax rate of $14.54
top_items.why: The board voted 4-1 to maintain a single tax classification rate rather than a split commercial rate, and voted 5-0 against residential and commercial exemptions.
top_items.body: Following a tax classification hearing with the Board of Assessors, the Select Board approved a single FY27 property tax rate of $14.54 per thousand of assessed value. Total town valuation grew to $4.072 billion, with the average single-family home valuation climbing 3.7 percent to $1,027,800. The adopted single rate results in an estimated 5.01 percent increase on the average single-family tax bill.

top_items.title: Neary School renovation estimates climb to $33M-$40M
top_items.why: Project architects determined an earlier $15 million budget cap is unfeasible because basic code and building system modernizations alone require $32.9 million.
top_items.body: Architects presented detailed cost models to the Elementary School Building Committee and School Committee regarding renovation options for Neary Elementary School. Baseline mechanical, civil, and building code upgrades are estimated at $32.9 million, while the preferred addition and renovation design—which constructs a full-sized gymnasium in the courtyard and modernizes learning spaces—totals approximately $39.8 million. Town officials are evaluating whether to pursue local financing or submit a Statement of Interest in January 2027 to seek state reimbursement through the Massachusetts School Building Authority.

top_items.title: Planning Board reviews Costco traffic, lighting, and environmental waivers
top_items.why: Costco's proposed 167,000-square-foot warehouse and gas station at 21 Coslin Drive faces regulatory review over intersection congestion and site waivers.
top_items.body: The Planning Board held two November hearings on Costco's site plan review and special permit applications. Board members and residents scrutinized traffic modeling around Route 9, vehicle queues, and cut-through truck traffic along residential streets, while also reviewing proposed dark-sky lighting, extensive tree plantings, and waiver requests for landscaping and stormwater infiltration. The public hearing was continued to December 14, 2026, with the board extending its decision deadline to December 18.

top_items.title: Select Board sponsors bylaw to eliminate 55-plus housing cap
top_items.why: The proposed zoning amendment lifts the municipal 7 percent cap on senior housing while mandating 12.5 percent affordability in new developments.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted to refer to the Planning Board and sponsor on the Town Meeting warrant a zoning bylaw amendment drafted by the Affordable Housing Trust. The measure removes Southborough's 7 percent cap on age-restricted developments, permits up to eight units per acre on parcels of at least two acres with 10 percent open space preservation, and mandates a minimum of 12.5 percent affordable units. The Zoning Board of Appeals also reviewed the draft, choosing to await Planning Board public hearings before considering a formal endorsement.

top_items.title: Town lands $632,000 state grant for Fayville Memorial Park redesign
top_items.why: A state Land and Water Conservation Fund grant will pay roughly half of the estimated $1.4 million park upgrade, reducing the local CPA request.
top_items.body: Southborough was awarded up to $632,000 in reimbursable state grant funding to construct a splash pad, dog park, walking trail, and accessibility improvements at Harold E. Fay Memorial Park. Because the grant functions on reimbursement, Town Meeting will still be asked to appropriate the full project cost using Community Preservation Act funds before state funds are returned to town accounts. Town boards are coordinating parking reconfigurations along Central Street and reviewing open space legal requirements ahead of the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Regional school district negotiates $450,000 health insurance savings
top_items.why: The Regional School Committee unanimously approved a Chapter 32B agreement with the Public Employee Committee to modify health plan designs.
top_items.body: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School District finalized statutory negotiations with its Public Employee Committee, securing health insurance changes that will yield approximately $450,000 in gross savings in FY28. Under state law, 25 percent of the savings ($126,000) will be set aside in a one-time subscriber mitigation fund, providing approximately $325,000 in net savings to reduce rising healthcare costs in the regional operating budget.
